provenance.evaluator: Second Run campaign (compiled from Run 3 session notes, campaign/results/RUN3-HOTAISLE-SUMMARY.md and availability/observations.jsonl)
provenance.account_used: existing Hot Aisle team account from the Second Run campaign (Run 3)
provenance.disclosure: Hot Aisle gave Second Run a $200 credit for these arms. The retained $15 estimate is a historical compilation with no reconciled invoice or precise allocation scope; it is not measured spend. List rate was $2.99/GPU-hr. Prospective commercial relationship disclosed in campaign/DISCLOSURES.md.

account_creation.notes: self-serve, no sales team (known campaign fact). Login is email + one-time code through the admin TUI (ssh admin.hotaisle.app) or the embedded web terminal; a registered SSH key can log into the TUI directly. Prepaid Stripe credits, $20 minimum -- a card is required to fund the account. Whether any request quota gate exists was never tested (no create was ever refused), so quota_gate is unobserved rather than assumed none.

price_transparency.notes: Public pricing page. 1x MI300X VM is $2.99/GPU-h with 1-minute minimum billing. 2x VM was $5.98/h with a 1-hour minimum observed on 2026-09-23. 8x bare metal is $3.39/GPU-h with a 1-month minimum. Egress and storage line items were never located on the pricing page or billed for.

provisioning.notes: Only one timed provisioning attempt exists in the campaign record (Run 3 seat enc1-gpuvm004: requested 00:08:55Z, SSH ready 00:10:57Z, 122s). It was not repeated 3 times in this session, so measured_3x is false; a dedicated counter run should time 3 creates at $2.99/GPU-hr with 1-minute minimum billing, well under the $3 budget for this step.

availability_honesty.notes: Mirrors availability/observations.jsonl rows with provider=hotaisle. Availability visibly changes: the TUI listing on 2026-09-23 showed only the 1x VM as available with a 'we're pretty full' banner (only 2x available on that weekday); more capacity was seen on weekends per prior campaign notes. Rows with method=tui-provision-list are listing observations, not create attempts -- only tui-provision (2026-09-24T00:10:45Z, seat enc1-gpuvm004) is a real delivered create. This ledger_attempts array mixes listed and delivered layers for a single honesty ratio; see availability/README.md for the two-layer distinction the canonical ledger keeps.

api_cli_tui_quality.notes: API token created self-serve and used as HOTAISLE_API_TOKEN by the campaign runner. `workload.cjs inspect` lists team/VM/state/balance (list_op). VM create and delete both exercised in the TUI during Run 3 (create_op, delete_op). Idempotency of repeated create/delete calls was never deliberately tested.

billing_granularity.billing_quantum: 1 minute minimum, then per-minute (1x MI300X VM); 1-hour minimum observed on the 2x VM
billing_granularity.notes: The VM was deleted from the TUI and billing stopped at delete (known campaign fact, per-run seat enc1-gpuvm004 deleted 2026-09-24T02:52:29Z per results/RUN3-HOTAISLE-SUMMARY.md). This was observed via account balance behavior around delete, not by reconciling a posted invoice line, so invoice_matches_balance stays unobserved.

tenant_hygiene.notes: Not checked in any prior session; a dedicated counter run should ssh in immediately after create and look for non-empty home directories, shell history, or authorized_keys entries not supplied by this evaluator.

network_path.notes: Seat enc1-gpuvm004 was reachable at a public IP (23.183.40.69) immediately after create. Default firewall posture and a first-boot port scan were never recorded.

support_path.notes: No support ticket was raised against Hot Aisle in any recorded session, so channel and response time are unobserved. sales_required is false on the strength of the repeated campaign fact 'self-serve, no sales team.'

termination.notes: VM deleted from the TUI; billing stops at delete (known campaign fact). Exact seconds between the delete action and the VM disappearing from the active list were not timed.
